clue.text: Cleopatra foolishly drinking in the morning — this to feel better?

indicators.note: a word drinking another takes it inside itself
letters arranged foolishly are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: AM (ante meridiem) means in the morning

explanation.surface: Cleopatra overdoes the morning tipple and asks what might fix her.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description: a hangover remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracetamol is a common painkiller taken for headaches and fever, so it is what you take to recover.

clue.text: Glimpse into a couple of pages reveals item that's disposable

indicators.note: one piece going into another sits inside it

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so two pages give PP
an aperçu is a glimpse or brief insight (French borrowing)

explanation.surface: A quick look at two pages exposes something meant to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: APERCU (without its accent) goes between the two Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper cup is a single-use drinking vessel, thrown away after use.

clue.text: Power couple, losing money, flare up again

parts.note: to reign is to hold power, as a ruler does

indicators.note: a word losing something has those letters taken away

parts.note: an item is a couple in a relationship
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 or M2

explanation.surface: A celebrity couple who go broke and then have a fiery row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power couple' reads as one celebrity phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reignite is literally to set alight once more, so a fire or quarrel flares anew.

clue.text: Witchy Woman roughly cut on Eagles' debut

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: circa means roughly or about, as with a date

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the word's first letter

explanation.surface: Witchy Woman, the Eagles hit, gets a rough cut on the band's first album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witchy Woman' is an Eagles song title, which steers toward the band, but it defines the sorceress of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe is the enchantress in the Odyssey who turns Odysseus's crew into pigs.

clue.text: "One Liberal removed from manipulated ballot papers" (The Sun?)

indicators.note: letters that are manipulated get rearranged
something removed from a word is taken out of it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal; one of the two is dropped
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about rigged ballot papers with a Liberal vote removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of BALLOT's two Ls goes ('removed from'); 'manipulated' rearranges the rest, BALOT, into TABLO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British popular daily, an example of a tabloid newspaper.

clue.text: Sheep tucking into pig's food could be a life-saver

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, here placed within the other word

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak, eaten by pigs
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep munching pigswill turns out, oddly, to save a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mae West was RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom actress.

clue.text: Utterly enjoy Mad

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
crazy means mad

explanation.surface: Reads as a fan's verdict on Mad magazine: totally loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like crazy is doing it intensely or to the utmost degree, a colloquial intensifier.

clue.text: Prince of Wales perhaps wasted last four of teenage years

indicators.note: wasted means lost, so the final four letters of the word go

parts.note: puberty is the time of growing up in the teenage years

explanation.surface: The heir to the throne frittered away the end of his teens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince of Wales' looks like royalty, but it is a common pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Wales is a frequent British inn sign, so it is an example of a public house.

clue.text: Blue flag protects vessel with fish, capsized in sticky substance

indicators.note: protects means wraps round, holding the other piece inside

parts.note: the Blue Peter is the blue signal flag hoisted before a ship sails

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the letters read the other way

parts.note: a tub is a vessel, as for bathing
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A naval flag shelters an overturned boat with its catch, all stuck in goo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' reverses the boat and fish together, giving ANUTBUT, before 'protects' wraps the flag round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a thick, gluey spread made from ground nuts.

clue.text: See 7
Previous head of religious community

definitions.meaning: a ... heads a priory, a house of monks or friars

explanation.surface: The former leader of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior is both an adjective for earlier and the title of a monastic superior.

clue.text: After separation, female accepted street food

parts.note: a break is a separation, as in a break-up
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: After a split, a woman settles for street food.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is a meal, the first food of the day.

clue.text: Rod made a phone call to ELO, for backing on record

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: rang means phoned
EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: backing means the letters go in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone rang the band ELO about backing vocals on their record.
explanation.walkthrough: ELO is the band Electric Light Orchestra; 'for backing' turns it into OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A range pole is a surveyor's striped staff used for sighting, a kind of rod.

clue.text: Pretty entertaining start to high jump

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so holding another piece inside

parts.note: cute means pretty

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pleasing take-off for a high jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high jump' looks like one sporting event; only 'jump' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Chute is short for parachute, and by extension a parachute drop or jump.

clue.text: Duet with nun terribly out of key

indicators.note: done terribly means badly, so letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A duet sung with a nun goes horribly off-pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An untuned instrument has not been adjusted to pitch, so it sounds off-key.

clue.text: No problem with Rushdie being supported

indicators.note: a problem with a word means its letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: A cheerful assurance that Salman Rushdie is being looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No problem' reads as one reassuring phrase; split it, and 'problem' becomes the anagram signal for the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to sustain with food, so nourished means sustained or kept going.

clue.text: Wrote a report that's incomplete in a rush

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: A reporter files a hurried, unfinished story.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to dash or race along, as in tearing down the road.

clue.text: See 17
Former politician's aide on call for NHS treatment

indicators.note: giving letters treatment works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's assistant phones for care on the National Health Service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state health service.
explanation.definitionFit: François Hollande was President of France from 2012 to 2017.

clue.text: Turn left twice on motorway to reach part of Scotland

indicators.note: the following pieces come straight after this one

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1
U stands for a U-turn

indicators.note: twice means the letter appears two times

explanation.surface: Driving directions: off the motorway, a U-turn and two lefts to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Unspecified bug blocked by IT service

indicators.note: a word blocked by another has it stuck in its middle

parts.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unnamed, catching illness

explanation.surface: An office complaint: some vague virus stopped by the IT department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like IT support, but it means church worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is a fixed form of public worship, a church service.

clue.text: Queen's Speech used by some to broaden one's horizon

indicators.note: some speakers' way of saying it gives the answer by ear

parts.note: to broaden your horizon is to see more

explanation.surface: The monarch's annual address used by some to widen their outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's Speech' is the state opening of Parliament; here it is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Seymour was Henry VIII's third wife and queen consort, mother of Edward VI.

clue.text: To start with, Sheffield United take on Spanish side — hard to believe

indicators.note: to start with means take the first letter

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football side

explanation.surface: Sheffield United taking on a Spanish club seems a fantasy fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and bizarre, so strange that it seems unbelievable.

clue.text: Mixture of old and new working capital

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A blend of tradition and modernity in a working capital.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Ordinary women in support of Andrew? That's essential!

indicators.note: in a down clue something in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: Andrew Marr is a British political journalist and broadcaster

explanation.surface: Ordinary women backing a man named Andrew, deemed indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Marr is a BBC political interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrow is the innermost core or essence of something, as in the marrow of the matter.

clue.text: Animal's acceleration between satisfactory and very good

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of the two other pieces

parts.note: OK means satisfactory
PI, short for pious, means very good
a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

explanation.surface: An animal's speed-up rated somewhere between fine and excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of Central Africa, related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Strong material Art composed with his partner's all the rage

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Art Garfunkel's partner was Paul Simon
in means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: Simon and Garfunkel's music, composed together, was hugely popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is heavy waterproof canvas used for covers.

clue.text: Bright star in clinical pharmacy

indicators.note: in shows the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: A star employee working at a hospital pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the label for the brightest star in a constellation, as in Alpha Centauri.

clue.text: Little known candidate's a nightmare?

definitions.meaning: an unexpected contender about whom little is known
a night mare, taken whimsically, is a horse in the dark

explanation.surface: The obscure candidate is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is an outsider in a race or election; literally, a mare at night is a horse in darkness.

clue.text: Point out it's a kind of kidney bean

indicators.note: out means not as normal, so the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: Someone pedantically notes a classification of bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinto is a speckled variety of the common bean, the same species as the kidney bean.

clue.text: These days North Korea's ready for revolution

indicators.note: revolution turns things round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the won is North Korea's currency, and ready means cash

explanation.surface: North Korea is primed for an uprising at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' as a noun is slang for money, as in 'ready cash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Now means at the present time, in these days.

clue.text: Exotic dancer surely not suitable for all Johnsons?

indicators.note: exotic means strange and unusual, so the letters are rearranged
not means the letter is left out

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer is surely not family viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnsons is a British chain of dry cleaning shops; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnsons is a well-known UK high-street firm offering garment cleaning services.
